content.title: About
content.content: Puffed chickpeas are dried chickpea seeds (Cicer arietinum) that have been quickly heated until they expand into a light, crunchy snack. They have a mild nutty flavor with a hint of sweetness and a texture similar to popcorn. The product is commonly enjoyed as a healthy snack, added to salads, granola, or baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chickpeas are one of the oldest cultivated legumes, grown for over 7,000 years.
Puffing is achieved by rapid heating, causing the moisture inside the seed to turn to steam and expand the grain.
Unlike many fried snacks, puffed chickpeas contain very little added fat because they are cooked without oil.
They are a popular source of plant protein and fiber among vegetarians and vegans.
In some cultures, puffed chickpeas are used in traditional dishes such as Indian papdi or Middle‑Eastern snack mixes.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A typical serving provides about 8 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar levels, and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with most fried snacks, puffed chickpeas are virtually fat‑free, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains thiamine, riboflavin, and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals and antioxidants
items.content: Provides iron, magnesium, zinc, and polyphenols that support immune function and oxidative balance.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chickpeas, ranging from mild skin symptoms to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can bind minerals and reduce their absorption; rotating chickpea consumption with other foods can mitigate this.

items.title: Possible gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause increased gas and bloating in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Puffed chickpeas can be eaten straight from the bag, tossed into salads, soups, yogurts, granola, used in baking, or as a crunchy topping for Asian‑style dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For extended shelf life, store in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent moisture absorption.
